Chapter 9: The Dance of Culture and Biology
When you look around at everything people have built—cities rising up, art on the walls, laws shaping lives, families growing and changing—it’s tempting to think that culture is somehow separate from biology. But here’s what the Red Queen teaches us: these two are always wrapped around each other, constantly shaping and reshaping our world.
Picture a classroom for a moment. Kids from all kinds of backgrounds gather in one room to learn and play. Some are naturally shy, others can’t wait to jump in. There are kids who love to get lost in stories, and others who light up when it’s time for math. The rules they follow, the games they invent, the dreams they hold—these are all touched by the world around them, but also by the deep, quiet rhythms of who they are inside.
In a way, you can think of culture as a new set of tools for running the Red Queen’s race. Traditions, taboos, clever innovations—they’re all ways we try to adapt, to find better ways to connect with each other and survive. But culture doesn’t erase our biology. Instead, it builds on top of it. Sometimes it turns up the volume, sometimes it softens those instincts, but it’s always working with what’s already there.
Let’s take the story of a community that treasures big families. In this place, having lots of children is seen as a blessing, a sign of happiness and success. But as life changes—more demanding jobs, longer years in school, the rising cost of just getting by—these values start to shift. Couples decide to have fewer children, but pour even more energy and love into each one. New kinds of families start to appear, and what it means to belong keeps evolving. The dance between biology and culture never really stands still, does it?
Most of the time, people don’t even realize how much of their lives are shaped by this back-and-forth. The longing for love, that ache of loneliness, the drive to find meaning—these aren’t just choices you make as an individual. They’re echoes of a much older story, written by both the world outside and the nature within.
